theory.intro: For a positive deposit and fixed positive rates, with no extra deposits or withdrawals, simple interest uses the **original deposit** each year. Compound interest uses the **current balance**, including earlier interest. Here compounding is annual.
facts: Simple interest is $I = Prn$, so the balance after $n$ years is $P + Prn$.
Compound interest is $FV = PV(1+r)^{n}$, so the interest earned is $FV - PV$.
With the same positive deposit and positive annual rate, simple and annually compounded balances are equal after one year; compound interest is greater after further whole years.
For positive rates, a higher simple rate can give more over a short term than a lower compound rate. Compare the totals for the stated term.
With a positive deposit and positive annual rates, the simple-interest balance is a straight line; the compound-interest balance curves upwards and gets steeper.
Work out each total in one calculation and round only at the end, or the difference shifts by cents.
steps: Find the total from the simple interest offer.
Find the total from the compound interest offer.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) $\$1200$ earns $5\%$ p.a. for $3$ years. Compare simple interest with annual compounding: how much extra interest does compounding earn, to the nearest cent?
(b) What is the difference if the same investment is held for only one year?
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $I=Prn$.
$I=1200\times0.05\times3$.
$I=\$180$.
$FV=PV(1+r)^n$.
$FV=1200(1.05)^3$.
$FV=\$1389.15$.
Compound interest $=1389.15-1200$.
Compound interest $=\$189.15$.
Extra interest $=189.15-180$.
Extra interest $=\$9.15$.
(b) Simple interest $=1200\times0.05\times1$.
Simple interest $=\$60$.
Compound interest $=1200(1.05)-1200$.
Compound interest $=\$60$.
Difference $=60-60$.
Difference $=\$0$.

workedExamples.question_text: A deposit of $\$3600$ can earn $8\%$ p.a. simple interest with $A$, or $7\%$ p.a. compounded annually with $B$. Compare their final balances (a) after $3$ years and (b) after $6$ years. Give each winning margin to the nearest cent.
$\$1800$ is invested for $3$ years at $10\%$ p.a. Complete the yearly ending balances for simple interest and annual compound interest.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Simple interest each year $=1800\times0.10$.
Simple interest each year $=\$180$.
Simple ending balance, year $1$: $1800+180=\$1980$.
Simple ending balance, year $2$: $1980+180=\$2160$.
Simple ending balance, year $3$: $2160+180=\$2340$.
Compound interest, year $1$: $1800\times0.10=\$180$.
Compound ending balance, year $1$: $1800+180=\$1980$.
Compound interest, year $2$: $1980\times0.10=\$198$.
Compound ending balance, year $2$: $1980+198=\$2178$.
Compound interest, year $3$: $2178\times0.10=\$217.80$.
Compound ending balance, year $3$: $2178+217.80=\$2395.80$.

$A$ is the simple interest account: its graph is a straight line.
Simple interest each year $=2000\times0.10=\$200$.
$B$ is the compound interest account: its graph curves upwards and gets steeper.
Compound interest, year $1$: $2000\times0.10=\$200$.
Compound ending balance, year $1$: $2000+200=\$2200$.
Compound interest, year $2$: $2200\times0.10=\$220$.
Compound ending balance, year $2$: $2200+220=\$2420$.
Compound interest, year $3$: $2420\times0.10=\$242$.
The compound account adds a larger amount of interest each year.

workedExamples.question_text: $\$4800$ earns $6.5\%$ p.a. compounded annually for $4$ years. Find the simple annual rate that earns the same total interest over those years, to two decimal places.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Compound interest $I=4800(1.065)^4-4800$.
For the same interest, $I=4800\times r\times4$.
$r=\dfrac{4800(1.065)^4-4800}{4800\times4}$.
As a percentage, $r\approx7.16\%$ p.a. Keep the unrounded compound interest when dividing.

workedExamples.question_text:
Two accounts each start with $\$4000$ at $5\%$ p.a. Their yearly ending balances are shown below. Find which account has the greater balance after year $3$, and by how much.

| Year | Simple interest | Annual compound interest |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $\$4200.00$ | $\$4200.00$ |
| $2$ | $\$4400.00$ | $\$4410.00$ |
| $3$ | $\$4600.00$ | $\$4630.50$ |
workedExamples.solution_text:
Read the two balances in the year $3$ row.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}4630.50-4600.00\\&=30.50\end{aligned}$

The compound account has the greater balance, by $\$30.50$.

foundation.question_text:
$\$8000$ is invested for $4$ years at $5\%$ p.a.
How much more interest does an account compounding annually earn than an account paying simple interest, to the nearest cent?

A credit union offers $6\%$ p.a. simple interest and a bank offers $6\%$ p.a. compounding annually.
$\$15\,000$ is invested with each for $3$ years.
Find the difference between the two final balances, to the nearest cent.

$\$6000$ is invested for $1$ year, one account at $7\%$ p.a. simple interest and one at $7\%$ p.a. compounding annually.
How much more interest does the compound account earn?
foundation.solution_text:
$I = 6000\times0.07\times1$
$=\$420$
$FV = 6000(1.07)^{1}$
$=\$6420$, so the compound interest is also $\$420$.
Difference $=420-420$
$=\$0$

foundation.question_text:
$\$4000$ is invested for $2$ years at $10\%$ p.a.
How much more interest does an account compounding annually earn than an account paying simple interest?

A bank offers $4.5\%$ p.a. simple interest and a credit union offers $4.5\%$ p.a. compounding annually.
$\$12\,000$ is invested with each for $5$ years.
How much more interest does the credit union account earn, to the nearest cent?

$\$2500$ is invested for $3$ years at $4\%$ p.a.
Complete the yearly ending balances for simple interest and annual compound interest.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc}\text{Year}&1&2&3\\\hline\text{Simple}&\ldots&\ldots&\ldots\\\text{Compound}&\ldots&\ldots&\ldots\end{array}$
foundation.solution_text:
Simple interest each year $=2500\times0.04=\$100$.
Simple ending balance, year $1$: $2500+100=\$2600$.
Simple ending balance, year $2$: $2600+100=\$2700$.
Simple ending balance, year $3$: $2700+100=\$2800$.
Compound interest, year $1$: $2500\times0.04=\$100$.
Compound ending balance, year $1$: $2500+100=\$2600$.
Compound interest, year $2$: $2600\times0.04=\$104$.
Compound ending balance, year $2$: $2600+104=\$2704$.
Compound interest, year $3$: $2704\times0.04=\$108.16$.
Compound ending balance, year $3$: $2704+108.16=\$2812.16$.

foundation.question_text:
$\$3000$ is invested for $3$ years at $10\%$ p.a.
Calculate the final balance with simple interest and with annual compound interest. Which gives the greater amount, and by how much?
foundation.solution_text:
$I=Prn$.
$I=3000\times0.10\times3$.
$I=\$900$.
$A=P+I$.
$A=3000+900$.
$A=\$3900$.
$FV=PV(1+r)^n$.
$FV=3000(1.10)^3$.
$FV=\$3993$.
Difference $=3993-3900$.
Difference $=\$93$.
Compound interest gives the greater final balance, by $\$93$.

development.question_text:
Bank A offers $7\%$ p.a. simple interest.
Credit union B offers $6\%$ p.a. compounding annually.
$\$9000$ is invested for $5$ years.
Which gives the greater final balance, and by how much, to the nearest cent?

Bank A offers $7\%$ p.a. simple interest and credit union B offers $6\%$ p.a. compounding annually.
$\$9000$ is invested for $10$ years.
Which gives the greater final balance, and by how much, to the nearest cent?
development.solution_text:
Bank A: $9000+9000\times0.07\times10$
$=\$15\,300$
Credit union B: $9000(1.06)^{10}$
$=\$16\,117.63$
Difference $=16\,117.63-15\,300$
$=\$817.63$
Credit union B gives the greater balance, by $\$817.63$.

development.question_text:
$\$6000$ is invested at $8\%$ p.a., once as simple interest and once compounding annually.
Find the difference between the two balances after $3$ years and after $6$ years, each to the nearest cent.
development.solution_text:
After $3$ years, simple balance $=6000+6000\times0.08\times3$.
Simple balance $=\$7440$.
Compound balance $=6000(1.08)^3$.
Compound balance $=\$7558.272$.
Difference $=7558.272-7440$.
Difference $\approx\$118.27$.
After $6$ years, simple balance $=6000+6000\times0.08\times6$.
Simple balance $=\$8880$.
Compound balance $=6000(1.08)^6$.
Compound balance $=\$9521.245937664$.
Difference $=9521.245937664-8880$.
Difference $\approx\$641.25$.

mastery.question_text:
$\$25\,000$ is invested at $6.4\%$ p.a. compounding annually for $6$ years.
Find the simple interest rate that would earn the same total interest over those $6$ years, correct to $2$ decimal places.
mastery.solution_text:
Compound interest $I=25000(1.064)^6-25000$.
For the same interest, $I=25000\times r\times6$.
$r=\dfrac{25000(1.064)^6-25000}{25000\times6}$.
Keep the full calculator value; as a percentage, $r\approx7.52\%$ p.a.

mastery.question_text:
$\$18\,000$ is invested at $7.5\%$ p.a. compounding annually for $4$ years.
Find the simple interest rate that would earn the same total interest over those $4$ years, correct to $2$ decimal places.
mastery.solution_text:
Compound interest $I=18000(1.075)^4-18000$.
For the same interest, $I=18000\times r\times4$.
$r=\dfrac{18000(1.075)^4-18000}{18000\times4}$.
Keep the full calculator value; as a percentage, $r\approx8.39\%$ p.a.
